readme:
明孝宗實錄 from scan to dated table

One 實錄 taken the whole way from the printed page to a table of dated records, with every step, its code, its output and its numbers kept. It is the worked example for the article (../docs/article/). JOURNAL.md tells the story in date order; this file is the map.

How the folder works

  • One folder per step. Each has a README.md (what, why, numbers, what went wrong), the code (run.py, run with uv run), the result in out/, and a manifest.json (input and output files with checksums).
  • There is no "before" copy in a step: the input of a step is the out/ of an earlier step, and the manifest names it.
  • A step never changes an earlier step's output. To fix something, fix that step and run everything after it again: for s in 03_pages_to_text 04_juan 05_months_and_records 06_dates; do uv run $s/run.py; done; uv run 07_review/build.py; uv run 08_table/run.py
  • A person's decisions are files (07_review/decisions/), applied by script.
  • The old base text and the old database are used only to check, never to fill in.
  • Shared code is in lib/ (numerals, 干支, the calendar, dating, manifests).

The steps

step what it does who decides check result (2026-11-10)
00_source the printed edition and its scan historian checksum of the PDF 4,310 pages
01_render PDF to page images script page count, checksums 4,310 images, 2,000 px
02_ocr images to text blocks (Chandra OCR 2 on the Mac mini) model smoke test of 2 models against the old text; loops counted 6 loops, 0 errors; median page differs 6.3% from the old text
03_pages_to_text margins apart, loops repaired, marks normalised rules mark counts per page against the old text 1.16 M characters; marks equal on 3,536 of 4,118 pages
04_juan cut into juan at the titles rule the 1966 margin label on every page 224 of 224 juan; label agrees on 3,948 of 4,128 pages (the rest are misread labels)
05_months_and_records month headers; records at ○ and △ rules every month of the calendar must be opened once, in order 221 of 221 months; 13,155 records
06_dates 干支 to JDN to Gregorian; every day of the reign beside the records; lost dividers calendar 朔 of each header; days against the old database 99.99% dated; 朔 agrees 216 of 218; 395 dividers restored
07_review the cases a rule cannot decide, as a review page historian none preselected 5 cards, all answered and applied
08_table the final table, one row per record script row counts 13,552 records, 6,526 days; 朔 218 of 218 after review
09_entities persons and places: Codex reads, scripts link to CBDB and TGAZ rules every string must be in its record; review of a sample 38,227 person and 25,758 place strings, none invented; 12,750 and 14,313 linked; links not yet reviewed (2026-11-14)
10_site a static website: the table, the persons and places, every page as read, and these steps script the site is opened and looked at built 2026-11-14

Where to look

  • The table: 08_table/out/xiaozong_records.csv (columns explained in 08_table/README.md).
  • Every day of the reign with its record count: 08_table/out/xiaozong_days.csv.
  • The review page: 07_review/out/xiaozong_review.html.

Needs from outside this folder

  • The scan: in the author's reference library (see 00_source/). Page images are not in git.
  • The calendar: cjk-calendar in humanities-skills (path in lib/reign_calendar.py).
  • For the checks only: ../original_data/mingshilu/xiaozong.txt and ../mingshilu.db.
journal:
孝宗實錄 from scan to database: the process log

This folder redoes the whole pipeline for one 實錄, 明孝宗實錄, starting from page images instead of from someone else's digital text. It is the worked example for the article (../docs/article/) and a sample we can publish. Every step is written down here when it happens: what was done, the command, the numbers, and what went wrong.

Why we start again from the scans

Our current 孝宗 text (224 juan, 1,215,754 characters) is the "base text": a digitisation of the 中研院 校勘本 whose origin and terms are unknown, and which still carries a few inline collation notes from that edition (for example 徵塞(塞閣本抱本作基)). We hold a scan of the printed edition itself. If we transcribe the Ming text from the scans ourselves, the transcription is our own work, of a public-domain text, and can be published.

Source

  • 明孝宗實錄, 劉健等修. 臺北: 中央研究院歷史語言研究所, 1966 (校印本; a photographic reproduction of the 國立北平圖書館藏紅格鈔本). The PDF is in the author's reference library.
  • PDF: 4,310 pages, 1634×2400 pt, scans only (no text layer). sha256 begins dcf25596040c084b.
  • Each page is one half-leaf of the manuscript: 10 columns of up to 20 characters, handwritten regular script. The margin gives 明孝宗實錄, the juan (卷一一〇), the leaf (五), and the 1966 edition's running page number (2015). Small marks in the outer margin point to the separate 校勘記; they carry no text.
  • Also at hand, not used for the text: 黃彰健, 明孝宗實錄校勘記 (1984). It is modern scholarship and stays a reference for checking only.

Log

2026-11-09 — test before the full run

  • Rendered 30 pages spread through the book (every 143rd page from page 70) at 2,000 px on the long side, with multi-agent-vision-ocr/scripts/render_pages.py. → smoke/img/
  • Sent them to the Mac mini (mini-jobs) on both local models: xz-smoke-surya (Surya 2.5, 8-bit MLX) and xz-smoke-chandra (Chandra OCR 2, 8-bit MLX).
  • Plan: score each page against our existing 孝宗 text, which is a second, independent witness, so its differences are a fair error estimate (an upper bound: some differences will be its errors, not the OCR's). Choose the model, then run all 4,310 pages.

Surya result (30 pages, about 4 minutes). First score: median 15.1% different from the old text. Looking at the differences showed the number was misleading, for three reasons, each now handled in scripts/score_pages.py:

  1. The margin (明孝宗實錄 卷二, leaf 三, page 0013) was counted as text. Surya labels it PageFooter; those blocks are now dropped. → median 11.2%.
  2. The manuscript and the old text use different variant forms. The commonest "errors" were Surya reading the manuscript correctly: 于 (old text 於, 24 times), 并 (並, 20), 陞 (升, 12), 勅 (敕), 鍾 (鐘), 復 (old text 複, a conversion error). Both sides are now also compared after folding to simplified (OpenCC t2s), which merges such pairs. → median 10.6%.
  3. The old text is often the wrong witness. On the two worst pages (lists of princes' names) it writes rare characters as two component characters (水禾, 木還, 金恩 for single characters: old 組字 encoding), writes 狹 for 陝 throughout, and has misreadings of its own. So the old text cannot be the answer key for hard pages.

Surya's own errors are look-alike characters: 論/諭, 秉/棗, 新/靳, 長/喪, 善/姜, 李刺/孛剌, 優/儀, 泰/秦. Three pages had almost no text (blank or title pages) and were not scored.

Chandra result (30 pages, 17 minutes; median 36 s a page, no loops). Chandra labels the margin Page-Header / Page-Footer and blank pages Blank-Page.

model raw median folded median folded mean better page
Chandra OCR 2 (8-bit) 8.5% 6.6% 8.0% 25 of 27
Surya 2.5 (8-bit) 11.2% 10.6% 11.1% 2 of 27

The two models differ from each other by 8.8% (folded median), so their errors are largely different ones: where both agree against the old text, the old text is probably wrong; where they disagree, a person or a third reader must look. The princes' name list (seq-4217) is bad for both (28% / 25%) and partly the old text's fault.

Decision proposed: Chandra for the whole book (about 4,310 × 36 s ≈ 43 hours), and Surya as a second reader (about 10 hours), so every page has two independent readings.

Decision (the author, 2026-11-09): Chandra 2 only, no second model.

2026-11-09 — full OCR run started

  • Rendered all 4,310 pages (PDF index 0–4309 → img/seq-0000.png … seq-4309.png), 2,000 px long side, greyscale; 986 MB, 8 min 45 s. uv run render_pages.py BOOK.pdf -o img --first 0 --long-side 2000
  • Sent to the mini: mini ocr img --name xiaozong-chandra (Chandra OCR 2, 8-bit MLX). Expected about 43 hours at 36 s a page. The two test jobs were pulled and forgotten first, to free the mini.

Lesson for the article: the old digital text is normalised, not diplomatic — it changed the manuscript's forms (于→於, 陞→升, 并→並) and encoded rare characters as component pairs. A fresh transcription keeps what the manuscript wrote.

2026-11-09 — first loops, and why they happen

At 954 of 4,310 pages: 2 loops, 0 errors, about 35 hours left (about 37 s a page).

Both loops have the same cause. Outside the printed frame, on the far left edge, some pages carry a short line of tiny print turned on its side (on seq-0891 it reads about "(一〇)R2", probably a film or plate label; on seq-0021 it is a faint smudge). Chandra reads it as a vertical column, one character per line, sees thin strokes as 一 or 〇, and repeats that character until it hits its limit of 12,384 tokens (about 11 minutes a page).

page content looping block stuck on seconds
seq-0021 table of contents, 卷之七–十二 Page-Footer, bbox x 0–21 〇 707
seq-0891 卷四〇, leaf 三 (page 0834) Page-Footer, bbox x 9–33 一 636

On both pages the main text was read in full before the loop: the table of contents is complete, and 卷四〇 runs through all ten columns to the last characters, 李福遣, with the page number 0834. Only the margin label was lost, and we drop it anyway.

Rules for the cleanup that follows from this:

  1. A loop is not always a lost page. If the looping block is a margin Page-Footer at the left edge and the text blocks before it are complete, keep the text and discard the looped block. Record which pages were treated this way.
  2. If a loop falls inside the main text, read the page again with the strip outside the frame cropped off.
  3. Keep counting. If many pages carry the side label, loops will grow and each costs about 11 minutes.

2026-11-10 — three more loops, this time in the main text

At 3,427 of 4,310 pages: 5 loops, 0 errors, about 9 hours left. The three new loops are of a different kind from the first two: they fall inside the main Text block, so the end of the page is lost.

page what the page is where it got stuck
seq-2015 a memorial by 南京禮部尚書 (人君之職莫大乎敬天…) repeats 敬天
seq-2326 list of princes' sons (第二子曰安洸…) repeats one son-entry pattern
seq-3036 list of princes' sons (嫡長子曰睦樞…) repeats one son-entry pattern

Cause: repetition in the text itself. The memorial repeats 敬天 as a theme word, and the name lists repeat the same pattern (嫡/庶, 第N子曰, 安-names) line after line. The model loses its place and keeps going round. These pages need a re-read (cropped into halves, so each read is shorter), and the name lists need a person's check in any case.

2026-11-10 — full run finished and pulled

  • xiaozong-chandra done: 4,310 of 4,310 pages, 6 loops, 0 errors. Total model time 43.1 hours; median 35.5 s a page (the smoke test forecast 36 s). Pulled to ocr/ (rows.jsonl, 5.8 MB, checksums match), then the job was forgotten on the mini.
  • Block labels: Text 5,000; Page-Footer 8,561; Page-Header 4,172; Section-Header 198 (juan titles and month headings); Blank-Page 36; Image 9; Table 1.
  • Record marks in the output: ○ 10,619, 〇 3,678, △ 303. The model writes the same manuscript circle in two Unicode forms (and 〇 is also the numeral zero in the margin), so marks must be normalised before cutting records.
  • Sixth loop, seq-3806 (卷二百二, 弘治十六年八月): a main-text loop on a list of princes' titles (鎮國將軍, 輔國將軍…), stuck on 後機. Same kind as seq-2326 and seq-3036. On this page the model also wrote △ for the record marks.

Score of the whole book against the old base text (uv run scripts/score_pages.py ocr): 4,170 pages scored; 140 not scored (blank, title or too short).

raw folded (variant forms merged)
median 7.89% 6.27%
mean 11.02% 9.49%

Folded rate by page: 1,467 pages ≤ 5%; 3,341 ≤ 10%; 4,046 ≤ 20%; 4,113 ≤ 40%. The median matches the smoke test (6.6%). The mean is pulled up by a few pages scoring over 100%: front matter the old text does not have (table of contents, seq-0008 to 0051, so the alignment fails), and the loop pages. Remember the rate is an upper bound: many differences are the old text's normalisations (于/於 and others), not OCR errors.

Next: re-read the 4 main-text loop pages in halves; then rebuild the text in page order.

2026-11-10 — the whole pipeline, steps 00 to 08

The folder was rebuilt as one folder per step (README.md is the map). Each step has its own README, code, out/ and manifest. The old img/, ocr/, smoke/, reread/ and scripts/ moved into 01_render/ and 02_ocr/. Steps 03 to 08 were written today, for this book only: small scripts, with the old pipeline's ideas but not its code.

What each step found (details and numbers in its README):

  • 03 The model wrote 4,947 full stops in a text that has none. On 356 pages 。 is its glyph for the record circle; on 293 pages it is punctuation the model added. Found because the circles were 2,000 short of the old text's. A second model (Surya, 26 pages) makes the same confusion. One blank page came back as an invented table.
  • 04 All 224 juan found from their titles. The 1966 margin label agrees on 95.6% of pages; the rest are misread labels.
  • 05 All 221 months opened in order. One misread year (元 as 九) had derailed a hundred juan until headers were tied to the calendar's order of months. In juan 50-58 and 183-202 the copyist marks the day on both sides (○辛巳○…): seen on the page image.
  • 06 13,497 of 13,498 records dated. 朔 agrees on 216 of 218 headers. The author's idea of laying every day of the reign (6,526) beside the records worked: 343 lost dividers were restored where a blank or a rising run of days made it certain, raising the days with records from 4,665 to 5,008; 55 more go to review. The old database has 303 of the 343 restored days.
  • 07 Review page with 116 cards. No decisions yet.
  • 08 08_table/out/xiaozong_records.csv: 13,498 rows.

Also: the last loop half (seq-3806a) looped again with Chandra and was read with Surya. The four test jobs were pulled and forgotten on the mini.

Open: the 116 review cards; records with no 干支 whose mark was lost (the calendar cannot see them); proofreading.

2026-11-10 — a third rule for lost dividers (the author's)

Rule: if a 干支 inside a record is the day right after the day before it, that day has no record, and the next record's day is the day right after it, then the 干支 begins a new record. It fills a one-day hole in a run of consecutive days, so no blank is needed. Added to lib/dating.py; steps 06 to 08 run again.

  • 29 more dividers restored (372 in all); the old database has a record on 22 of those 29 days. Days with records: 5,037. Records: 13,527.
  • Review cards for lost dividers fall from 55 to 26; the page now has 87 cards.

2026-11-10 — the consecutive-day rule, extended to one side

The author looked at review cards where the 干支 follows the previous day directly but the days after it are empty, and asked for the rule to cover them. Now one side is enough: the 干支 is the day right after the previous dated record, or the day right before the next one (at a month's end: before the first day of the next month).

  • 23 more dividers restored (395 in all). Rule 3 now accounts for 52; the old database has a record on 43 of those 52 days.
  • Days with records 5,060; records 13,550. Lost-divider cards: 3 (empty days on both sides). One of them, 上以戊申紀元, is a year, which shows why that case is not automatic.
  • Review page: 64 cards.

2026-11-10 — flagged 干支 settled by rule

The author's view: a 干支 that breaks the order or is no day of its month is not a divider. For a 干支 inside a record that was already the rule. For the 59 that open a record after a mark, the data showed most are real days misread by the OCR (47 had exactly one empty day beside them that differs by one character). Agreed rule:

  • one empty day fits, one character different: correct to that day, keep the reading, note it. 46 corrected; the old database has a record on 28 of those days.
  • otherwise: not a date. 13 records keep the previous day and stay flagged. Some of these look like real days misread in both characters (庚午文武羣臣朝親王…); they wait for proofreading against the page.

Days with records 5,106; still empty 1,420. The review page is down to 5 cards (3 lost dividers, 2 朔).

2026-11-10 — first review applied

The author answered all 5 cards (07_review/decisions/xiaozong_review_results_2026-11-10.json). Step 08 applied them: two more dividers (乙卯 in juan 64, 辛亥 in juan 123), 上以戊申紀元 left alone, and both differing 朔 confirmed as OCR misreads (丙午, 辛丑), so every one of the 218 朔 now agrees with the calendar. Final table: 13,552 records, 13,551 dated, 5,108 of 6,526 days with records.

2026-11-10 — the 13 "not a date" records checked against the day table and the pages

Full table: 06_dates/flagged_check_2026-11-10.md.

  • Pages out of order in the scan. Two flagged days in juan 20 (壬申, 庚午) were right. Scan pages seq-0525 to 0527 carry printed numbers 0470, 0469, 0468: the three pages are reversed. Step 03 now checks the printed page number against the scan position for the whole book and puts such pages back. Nowhere else is affected.
  • 1 real day misread in both characters (己未科 for 癸巳六科): corrected from the page.
  • 6 are not dates; the OCR made 命成, 昏刻, 內閣, 茂陵, 虜入, 以上 look like 干支. The dating rule was right; the text of those records is wrong.
  • 3 are out of order in the manuscript itself (乙亥 after 戊寅; 癸未 after 乙酉; 辛酉 after 壬戌), and the old text reads the same. For the 校勘記.

Lesson for the article: a date check finds more than date errors. Here it found a binding or scanning fault, OCR misreadings of ordinary words, and three slips of the Ming copyist.

Final table: 13,552 records, 13,551 dated, 5,111 of 6,526 days with records.

2026-11-11 — a false "corrected by the calendar" day, found while drawing a figure

Record 121-0010 (弘治十年正月, seq-2224). The page reads ○以大祀 天地. The OCR read 以 as 戊午, and the one-character rule then "corrected" it to 戊申, an empty day. So the record has a day it should not have; it belongs to 丁未, as the old database has it. This is the same misreading as 以上元節 → 己未元節 among the 13 checked on 2026-11-10, but here the rule accepted it. Not changed yet. Of the 46 corrections the old database has a record on 28 days; the other 18 need a look at the page before the rule is trusted.

2026-11-13 — step 09 begins: persons and places, pilot of 200 records

The author's rulings: persons and places only, no offices; CBDB and TGAZ only, no Wikidata; disambiguate, and record everything. The reader is Codex (gpt-6-astra), not a Claude subagent; linking is by script.

  • 200 records, 8 batches. Codex returned 919 person strings and 726 place strings. None was absent from its record.
  • Linked: 253 persons (90 strong, 76 medium, 87 weak), 371 places. Not in CBDB 284; not in TGAZ 354; ambiguous persons 131.
  • Found on the way: 趙氏 was linked to a CBDB person. Surname + 氏 is no longer looked up. Princes appear without 朱 (見溥); a second lookup with 朱 is made and marked weak.
  • Review page with 69 cards built; not yet answered. Recall not measured.
  • Cost of the pilot: 208k tokens in, 24k out, about 4 minutes.

2026-11-14: step 09, full run

  • Codex read all 13,552 records in 544 batches (3 at a time, about 2.4 hours). All answered; no string outside its record.
  • Tokens: 12.2M in (9.2M of them cached), 1.13M out.
  • Persons: 38,227 strings; 11,855 linked (strong 4,324, medium 3,355, weak 4,176); 11,066 not in CBDB; 6,525 ambiguous; 2,608 no candidate fits the date; 6,173 not looked up (titles, one-character names, surname + 氏).
  • Places: 25,758 strings; 14,313 linked (strong 4,084, medium 7,716, weak 2,513); 11,374 not in TGAZ; 71 ambiguous.
  • Known weak points, not fixed: 劉健 and 劉吉 (grand secretaries) are left ambiguous; 通州, 甘州, 肅州, 涼州, 臨清 are reported as not in TGAZ and need a look; 孔子 is not matched (CBDB has 孔丘).
  • Precision not measured. Review page: 09_entities/full/review/entities_review.html (87 cards).

2026-11-14: step 09, second pass for ambiguous persons

  • New rule in link.py: a name left ambiguous takes the candidate that office evidence chose for the same name in at least 3 other records of the reign, if that candidate is among those kept and no other kept candidate was ever chosen that way. Method office-elsewhere, confidence weak, vote count written in candidates.csv.
  • Effect on the full run: 895 mentions of 137 names moved from ambiguous to linked (劉健 53, 李興 49, 張海 36, 劉吉 26 ...). Persons linked 11,855 -> 12,750; ambiguous 6,525 -> 5,630. No Codex call was needed.
  • Still ambiguous: 馬誠 65, 楊偉 53, 周景 46 and others, where the record never names an office CBDB knows.
  • Places: 通州, 甘州, 肅州, 涼州 and 臨清 are missing because TGAZ has no record of them for the Ming years, only for earlier periods or 1820/1911. Not a script fault; nothing changed.

2026-11-14: step 10, the website

  • 10_site/build.py builds a static site from the step outputs: the table with persons and places, every page as read (cleaned text and the model's raw answer), one page per step (README, numbers, manifest, code, sample output), this journal and the files to download. 80 files, 58.6 MB.
  • Published to GitHub Pages: repo kltng/xiaozong-shilu (public, holds only the built site), https://kltng.github.io/xiaozong-shilu/. To update: uv run build.py && sh publish.sh "what changed".
  • Not on the site: the page images, the old base text, Codex's event logs, job logs. The pages carry noindex.
  • A first plan to serve it from our own server was dropped at the author's word before anything was deployed.

2026-11-15: step 09, an experiment with a local reader (Qwen3.8 27B)

  • Question: can an open model on our own laptop do the reading that Codex did? Same 200 pilot records, same prompt.md, same schema.json; only the reader changes. Scripts: 09_entities/extract_local.py, compare.py. Run folder: 09_entities/pilot_qwen/.
  • Reader: qwen3.8:27b from the Ollama library (18 GB, 4-bit), on an M1 Max laptop with 64 GB, temperature 0, thinking off, one batch at a time. The download failed twice on network timeouts before it went through.
  • Time: 19 minutes for the 8 batches (1,142 s; Codex: about 4 minutes with three at once). 43,872 tokens in, 42,603 out. All 8 answers valid.
  • Persons: Qwen returned 710 strings, Codex 919; 659 are the same. Qwen invented 1 (魏驥), Codex 0. Linked to CBDB: Qwen 207, Codex 253; 203 record-and-person pairs are linked by both.
  • Places: Qwen 709, Codex 726; 595 the same. Qwen invented 1 (南京 in a record that does not have it). Linked to TGAZ: Qwen 355, Codex 371; 342 pairs by both.
  • What Qwen missed: one-character and given-name-only mentions (祐, 宏, 忱), many titles (皇太后, 樂安王), and long lists (record 115-0034: 29 persons missed; 139-0044: 17 places). What Qwen added wrongly: palace buildings, offices and general words as places (乾清宮, 內閣, 禮部, 天下, 午門), against rule 3 of the prompt.
  • Not judged: which reader is right where they differ. That needs the review page.

2026-11-15: the website in three languages

  • The site now reads in English, Traditional Chinese and Japanese (10_site/i18n/). Labels: 220 short texts in ui.json. Notes: 15 files (the READMEs of steps 00 to 09, the top README, this journal, TIME.md, the flagged-干支 check, the Qwen experiment) translated by a language model from cleaned English copies, so nothing private went to the translators.
  • Checked by script: each translation has the same headings, table rows, list items and code spans as its English, and the same numbers except where a unit was changed (12.2 million became 1,220 萬). Not checked by a person; the About page says so, and says the English is the record.
  • Not translated: the 實錄 text, the prompt, code, sample data, figures, the two review pages.
  • Also added: a page that compares Codex and Qwen on the 200 pilot records (#/compare).
time:
Time used, steps 00 to 09

From the first test page to the full run of persons and places: six calendar days, 9 to 14 November 2026. Almost all of the measured time is machine time, and most of that is the OCR, which ran unattended.

Machine time, measured

step what ran time
00 Source nothing to run none
01 Render PDF to 4,310 page images 8 min 45 s
02 OCR, tests a 30-page test on two models, re-reads of looped pages, a test of the marks 35 min
02 OCR, full run Chandra OCR 2 on one Mac mini (M4, 16 GB), 4,310 pages, median 35.5 s a page 43.1 hours
03 to 08 the scripts, run one after another about 3 minutes
07 Review the historian's five cards not recorded
09 Codex, pilot 8 batches, 200 records 3 min
09 Codex, full run 544 batches, 13,552 records, three at a time 2.4 hours on the clock (7.2 model-hours)
09 Linking scripts that look names up in CBDB and TGAZ not timed; a few minutes
all about 46.5 hours on the clock
  • The OCR is 93% of the machine time.
  • The 3 minutes for steps 03 to 08 is one clean run, taken from the time stamps of the output files. The scripts were written and run many times before that; those runs were not recorded.
  • Codex used 12.2 million tokens in (9.2 million of them cached) and 1.13 million out.

Working time of the historian and the AI agent, a rough estimate

The log of the working session shows about 3.3 hours of active exchange between the historian and the AI agent over five working days (0.6, 1.0, 0.4, 0.7 and 0.6 hours). Only gaps of five minutes or less between messages were counted.

This number is weak in two ways. It includes other work done in the same session (an article draft, figures, this website). And it leaves out every stretch where the agent worked for more than five minutes without a message, and the historian's time reading pages and answering review cards away from the chat. So there is no clean figure for human time. The safest statement is: about 46 hours of unattended machine time, and a few hours of the historian's attention spread over five working days.

Token price

Only step 09 used a paid language model by the token. The OCR (step 02) ran on our own Mac mini with an open model, so it has no token price. Steps 03 to 08 are scripts.

Codex ran on a ChatGPT subscription, so no per-token charge was paid. The table shows what the same tokens would cost at OpenAI's list price for the API, for the model used (gpt-6-astra, standard rate, read from OpenAI's model page on 2026-11-14): $10 per million input tokens, $1 per million cached input tokens, $50 per million output tokens.
